Лапка для Python — не звичайний символ,: A quotation mark for Python is not an ordinary character, but a line boundary: the first quotation mark opens the line, the same one closes it. Therefore, in print("He says: "Hello""), Python will close the line before the word Hello and stop the program with a SyntaxError. In order for the quotation mark to become part of the text, a backslash is placed in front of it: \" — this is called escaping. There is a trick without a slash: to take the text in quotation marks of a different type — double quotation marks inside single ones are not considered a boundary, as well as an apostrophe inside double ones. But when the text contains both quotation marks and apostrophes, one pair will have to be escaped anyway. Another trick is to break the text into pieces and glue them through +, but the line becomes long and it's easy to lose a quotation mark in. Escaping leaves the text as a whole, which is read exactly as it is written, so it is shorter and more reliable.
